body:
I think you have misread the documentation, where did you find this? It says this in the documentation:
> Changing the Z index of a `Control` only affects the drawing order, not the order in which input events are handled.

Are you maybe thinking about this:
> For UI elements specifically, it makes more sense to override the virtual method `_gui_input()`, which filters out unrelated input events, such as by checking z-order, mouse_filter, focus, or if the event was inside of the control's bounding box.

This is quite confusingly phrased, but it does not take it into account from what I can find, and isn't designed to

See:
* https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/85305

This wording needs to be adjusted

Yeah that's what I was referring to. 

I've read the issue you linked. In that case, I think this should be filed as a documentation bug.

Also, this behavior unfortunately makes some ideas harder to implement. One idea I saw was, in a 3D project, to unproject the position of 3D elements and use that and Control nodes to place complex 2D UI elements above said 3D element (names of characters for example) This idea works to display information, but if you require this UI to be interactive (be able to click the name) then there will be a lot of z-fighting if multiple controls are close together.

Edit: That section of the documentation says it checks z-order and bounding box. Well, it doesn't check z-order but it does check the bounding box. For example, _unhandled_input catches inputs outside of the area of the control but _gui_input filters them. In your link the issue mentioned z-order isn't checked for performance reasons. Why is checking z-order (checking which number is greater) less efficient than checking the bounding box?

Anyway, if there's nothing to add about this then the issue can be closed. Thanks for the information.
